sourceIssues.reason: With |v| = Inf{α^n : t^n v ∈ V} as in (2), v lies in V exactly when n = 0 is allowed, that is, when |v| ≤ α⁰ = 1. sourceIssues.printed: "The t-adic completion of R_U is R̂_U = k[x][[t]]; we have F_U = Frac(R̂_U) = k(x)((t))."
sourceIssues.correction: Frac(k[x][[t]]) is a proper subfield of k(x)((t)). The erratum says this but gives the witness Σ_{n≥1} t^n/x^n, which lies in Frac(k[x][[t]]). A valid witness is Σ_{n≥1} t^n/x^{n!}.
sourceIssues.reason: The erratum's series equals t/(x − t), since 1/(x − t) = Σ_{n≥0} t^n/x^{n+1} in k(x)((t)), and x − t ∈ k[x][[t]]; so it is not in the complement. A correct witness: for c = a/b with a, b ∈ k[x][[t]], remove the common power of t so that b_0 ≠ 0, and let m = ord_x(b_0). The recursion c_n = (a_n − Σ_{i≥1} b_i c_{n−i})/b_0 gives ord_x(c_n) ≥ −m(n + 1). Every element of Frac(k[x][[t]]) therefore has x-poles growing at most linearly in n, while Σ t^n/x^{n!} has poles of order n!. The paper's general arguments use F_U = Frac(R̂_U), not this identification. Noted by the extraction, which also found the flaw in the erratum's witness.

sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 4.4(2): "The Tits index Δ_0(G) is the smallest subset of Δ(G_{F_s}) which is stable under the ⋆-action of Gal(F_s/F) and such that Δ_0(G) ⊂ Δ_0(G_{F_U}) for each U ∈ U and Δ_0(G) ⊂ Δ_0(G_{F_P}) for each P ∈ P." Corollary 4.5(2) is worded the same way. The proof defines Θ by the same condition and uses "Θ ⊂ Δ_0(G_{F_U}) so that Z(F_U) ≠ ∅".
sourceIssues.correction: Δ_0(G) is the smallest ⋆-stable subset Θ of Δ(G_{F_s}) with Δ_0(G_{F_U}) ⊂ Θ for each U and Δ_0(G_{F_P}) ⊂ Θ for each P, and similarly in Corollary 4.5(2). In the proof, use Δ_0(G_{F_U}) ⊂ Θ, which is what makes Par_Θ have an F_U-point.
sourceIssues.reason: Δ_0 is the type of a minimal parabolic subgroup under the order-preserving correspondence I ↦ P_I (p.2). Over an extension field minimal parabolics shrink, so Δ_0(G_{F_U}) ⊂ Δ_0(G). A parabolic of type Θ exists over a field L exactly when Δ_0(G_L) ⊂ Θ. As printed, the "smallest ⋆-stable subset contained in all the local Δ_0" is the empty set, and the defining condition refers to Δ_0(G) itself. With the inclusions reversed, the statement follows from part (1) applied to Par_Θ, as the proof intends. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (gap G3).

sourceIssues.printed: "We apply now Theorem 1.1.(b) of [C-G-R] to the Z-group scheme Aut_I(G_0). It provides a finite Z-subgroup S_0 of Aut_I(G_0) … Furthermore the construction of S_0 is explicit in the proof, it is an extension of the finite constant group Aut_I(G_0)/T_0 by a finite subgroup of T_0."
sourceIssues.correction: "… an extension of the finite constant group N_{Aut_I(G_0)}(T_0)/T_0 by a finite subgroup of T_0."
sourceIssues.reason: Aut_I(G_0) contains the adjoint group of G_0, so Aut_I(G_0)/T_0 is not finite. The finite group produced by the construction of Chernousov–Gille–Reichstein is the normalizer quotient, an extension of the diagram automorphisms stabilizing I by the Weyl group. Its order is what the hypothesis on p controls.
